model: AFFO-holding-period at cost of equity (REIT/property-trust row): 5-year attributable AFFO/dividend stream discounted at CoE, terminal value = exit P/B x projected NAV/share constrained to the observed listed-history P/B band; cross-checked by direct Gordon capitalization of normalized attributable AFFO at CoE and by NAV-with-exit-discount. NOT an owner-FCF DCF.

inputs.share_count_basis: 146,497,193 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (HY26 presentation p.4 fn.3); held FLAT -- buyback authorised but dormant, DRP now discretionary per dividend; performance-fee shares and any DRP issuance are a drag inside the NAV/share growth assumption, not double-charged via share count
inputs.net_debt_treatment: DISCLOSED ONLY — NOT deducted. AFFO is post-interest; capitalizing it at cost of equity already prices the $132.717m bank debt. Deducting net debt again would double-count it.
inputs.lp_units_treatment: Roc Partners' ~25% economic interest in the land-owning LP ($78.101m at 30 Jun 2026, non-current liability). Charged EXACTLY ONCE: the flows are NZL-ATTRIBUTABLE AFFO, not consolidated AFFO. NAV/share $1.5972 (net assets $233.990m) is ALREADY after the LP-unit liability, so it is not deducted again. Note Roc's share of consolidated AFFO rose to 34% in HY26 (1.880 of 5.467) because income tax, corporate overheads and corporate-level interest fall on NZL's side only.
inputs.last_fcf_definition: Trailing-twelve-month AFFO attributable to NZL shareholders to 30 June 2026: FY2025 7.932 - HY25 3.911 + HY26 3.587 (5.18 cps as 2.73 H2-25 + 2.45 H1-26). FY2025 full year was 7.932 (5.43 cps).

Left inside AFFO -- recurring income on the trust structure's loan receivables; the company's AFFO definition already strips the non-cash capitalised interest ($0.732m in HY26). Part of HY26 finance income was earned on the $8.355m advanced property settlement, which converted to owned orchard land (rent) in July 2026.

base.rationale: FY26 = 2.45 cps H1 actual + ~2.00 cps H2 estimate (H1 run-rate less Hawke's Bay rent of $1.36m/yr from July, less the ~$0.28m of H1 tax that residual losses sheltered, less part of the $0.7m Kiwi Crunch arrears and vacancy holding costs; plus June CPI reviews and seven weeks of interest saved). FY27 4.90 cps = normalised run-rate: Hawke's Bay rent gone, NZ$18.84m of debt repaid (~$0.9m/yr interest), full-year cash tax, CPI reviews. That is ~15% below the prior base FY27 of 5.75 cps. FY28-FY30 growth 4.0/3.5/3.0% UNCHANGED from the prior version for the same fiscal years, FY31 extended at 3.0%. NAV: Dec-26 start $1.58 = 30 Jun actual 1.5972 less ~2 cps for NZL's 75% share of the Hawke's Bay sale below book (sold NZ$18.84m vs $23.07m carried at Dec-25, $0.7m already written down in H1); growth 1.0%/yr unchanged. Exit P/B CHANGED 0.63 -> 0.60: with AFFO per dollar of NAV structurally lower after tax, holding 0.63 would price the exit at a ~5.3% AFFO yield, richer than the stock has traded; 0.60 puts the exit on ~5.6%, in line with today's trailing yield, and sits between today's 0.56x and the listed-history mean.

bull.rationale: FY26 4.65 cps (arrears largely recovered, no holding-cost drag); Board holds the 1.34 cps quarterly dividend through H2 (stub 2.68 cps). FY27 5.10 cps: sale proceeds redeployed accretively, MM Forests and South Island Orchards arrears cured. Growth 5.0/4.5/4.0% for FY28-FY30 unchanged from the prior version, FY31 at 4.0%. Dec-26 NAV $1.60 (dairy-land revaluations offset the orchard loss), NAV growth 2.5%/yr and exit P/B 0.74 (the historical maximum, needing a corporate catalyst: buyback execution, internalisation or takeover) all unchanged. Note the exit then sits on a ~4.5% AFFO yield, which only a NAV-based transaction, not yield investors, would pay.

Growth 3.0/3.0/2.5% for FY28-FY30 unchanged, FY31 at 2.5%. Dec-26 NAV $1.55, NAV -1.5%/yr, exit P/B 0.52 and payout 90% unchanged.

cost_of_equity_build.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY (not WACC): AFFO is post-interest so debt is priced inside the flow. NZD flows at NZD-derived rates. UNCHANGED from the 2026-08-23 version: base 9.25% = NZ 10yr risk-free 4.40% + rural-land asset-class equity premium 3.10% + NZX small-cap illiquidity premium 1.00% + tenant-concentration/credit premium 0.50% + short-debt-tenor refinancing premium 0.25%; bull 8.75%, bear 10.50%. The risk-free rate was NOT re-sourced for this update. Evidence since then cuts both ways and is judged to net out: the Kiwi Crunch exposure is crystallised by sale and debt tenor lengthened to 2.3 years (lower risk), but arrears have appeared at two more tenants holding 7.3% of rent and hedge cover slipped to 91% (higher risk). Market-implied cross-check: trailing attributable AFFO yield of about 5.8% plus ~3% per-share growth gives roughly 8.8%, so base CoE still sits above market-implied.
cost_of_equity_build.what_would_move_it: A re-sourced NZ 10-year yield more than ~50bp from 4.40%; a further tenant insolvency (credit premium up); renewal of the remaining short-dated tranches (refinancing premium out).

Bear stays elevated above the house 15%: the Kiwi Crunch exposure is now crystallised (orchards sold, settled 10 Nov 2026), but rent arrears have since been disclosed at MM Forests (2.7% of LP rent) and South Island Orchards (4.6%, plus $2.6m separately owing), the H1 dividend exceeded H1 AFFO, and guidance is still suspended. affo_capitalization_cross_check.reconciles: The holding-period base ($0.849) now sits about 13% ABOVE the Gordon capitalization ($0.754); the gap was ~7% in the prior version. It widened because the cash-tax step-down hits a pure yield capitalization in full, while three-quarters of the holding-period value is exit P/B x NAV, which AFFO does not touch. Trimming the base exit P/B to 0.60 closes part of it; the rest is a real disagreement between a yield lens and a book lens, and KPMG's review says investors use the yield lens. Read the base IV as the upper half of the fair-value range, not its midpoint.

valuation_philosophy: NZL's discount to NAV (about 44% today) is treated as STRUCTURAL, not a mispricing to be harvested. Evidence: (1) the stock has never closed a fiscal year above 0.74x book in its listed life, including at IPO; (2) the February-2026 KPMG capital review found investors price NZL on cash yield with NAV a secondary consideration; (3) external management fees are the classic driver of persistent NAV discounts; (4) OIO farmland screening shrinks both the asset exit-buyer pool and the corporate takeout pool -- though the Hawke's Bay sale to a Craigmore-managed partnership did clear OIO within about three months; (5) the buyback has stayed at zero through the widest discount. The valuation therefore capitalizes ATTRIBUTABLE cash yield at cost of equity and exits at an in-band P/B. What changed in this update is the yield itself: NZL exhausted its tax losses and became a cash taxpayer in HY26, so attributable AFFO/share stepped down (2.45 cps vs 2.70) even as rents rose, and the 1.34 cps quarterly dividend is no longer covered. The minority is charged exactly once: attributable AFFO in the flows; NAV already nets the LP-unit liability.
